papers.title: Study on Surface Roughness, Morphology, and Wettability of Laser-Modified Powder Metallurgy-Processed Ti-Graphite Composite Intended for Dental Application.
papers.abstract: In this study, the surface laser treatment of a new type of dental biomaterial, a Ti-graphite composite, prepared by low-temperature powder metallurgy, was investigated. Different levels of output laser power and the scanning speed of the fiber nanosecond laser with a wavelength of 1064 nm and argon as a shielding gas were used in this experiment. The surface integrity of the machined surfaces was evaluated to identify the potential for the dental implant's early osseointegration process, including surface roughness parameter documentation by contact and non-contact methods, surface morphology assessment by scanning electron microscopy, and surface wettability estimation using the sessile drop technique. The obtained results showed that the surface roughness parameters attributed to high osseointegration relevance (Rsk, Rku, and Rsm) were not significantly influenced by laser power, and on the other hand, the scanning speed seems to have the most prevalent effect on surface roughness when exhibiting statistical differences in all evaluated profile roughness parameters except Rvk. The obtained laser-modified surfaces were hydrophilic, with a contact angle in the range of 62.3° to 83.2°.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究粉末冶金钛-石墨复合材料的激光表面处理，未涉及增材制造、应力遮挡或疲劳测试。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not involve LPBF fabrication, porous structures, stress shielding, or mechanical/fatigue testing, which are central to the AM biomedical materials direction.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究激光处理钛-石墨复合材料的表面特性以促进牙植入体骨整合。
summary_zh.method: 使用纳秒光纤激光在不同功率和扫描速度下处理Ti-graphite复合材料，并通过接触和非接触方法评估表面粗糙度、形貌和润湿性。
summary_zh.result: 扫描速度显著影响粗糙度参数，表面呈亲水性，接触角62.3°至83.2°。
summary_zh.validation: 无力学性能验证，仅表面表征。

summary_en.motivation: This study investigates laser surface modification of a Ti-graphite composite for dental implants to enhance early osseointegration through controlled roughness and wettability.
summary_en.method: A fiber nanosecond laser at varying power and scanning speed was applied to Ti-graphite composite surfaces, with roughness measured by contact and non-contact methods, morphology by SEM, and wettability by sessile drop technique.
summary_en.result: Scanning speed significantly influenced roughness parameters, while all laser-modified surfaces were hydrophilic with contact angles between 62.3° and 83.2°.
summary_en.validation: No mechanical testing or fatigue evaluation was performed; only surface characterization was conducted.

papers.title: Predicting the hyperelastic properties of alginate-gelatin hydrogels and 3D bioprinted mesostructures.
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing has been widely used in tissue engineering, as 3D bioprinting enables fabricating geometrically complicated replacements for different tissues and organs. It is vital that the replacement mimics the specific properties of native tissue and bears the mechanical loading under its physiological conditions. Computational simulations can help predict and tune the mechanical properties of the printed construct-even before fabrication. In this study, we use the finite element (FE) method to predict the mechanical properties of different hydrogel mesostructures fabricated through various print patterns and validate our results through corresponding experiments. We first quantify the mechanical properties of alginate-gelatin hydrogels used as matrix material through an inverse approach using an FE model and cyclic compression-tension experimental data. Our results show that the fabrication process can significantly affect the material properties so that particular caution needs to be paid when calibrating FE models. We validate our optimized FE model using experimental data and show that it can predict the mechanical properties of different mesostructures, especially under compressive loading. The validated model enables us to tune the mechanical properties of different printed structures before their actual fabrication. The presented methodology can be analogously extended for cell bioprinting applications, other materials, and loading conditions. It can help save time, material, and cost for biofabrication applications in the future.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文使用有限元方法预测生物打印结构的力学性能，但未涉及AI/ML方法。
llm.why_not_core: No AI/ML method used; purely physics-based FEA without surrogate or machine learning.

summary_zh.motivation: 在制造前预测并调谐生物打印结构的力学性能。
summary_zh.method: 采用有限元逆分析和循环压缩实验量化海藻酸钠-明胶水凝胶的力学参数。
summary_zh.result: 验证的有限元模型能准确预测不同打印图案的压缩力学响应。
summary_zh.validation: 通过循环压缩-拉伸实验数据验证有限元模型预测结果。

summary_en.motivation: To predict and tune the mechanical properties of 3D bioprinted constructs before fabrication using computational simulation.
summary_en.method: An inverse finite element approach was used to calibrate hyperelastic material parameters from cyclic compression-tension experiments on alginate-gelatin hydrogels.
summary_en.result: The validated FE model accurately predicted the compressive mechanical behavior of printed mesostructures with different infill patterns.
summary_en.validation: Experimental cyclic compression tests on hydrogel specimens and printed structures validated the FE model predictions.

papers.title: A Meshless Solver for Blood Flow Simulations in Elastic Vessels Using Physics-Informed Neural Network
papers.abstract: Investigating blood flow in the cardiovascular system is crucial for assessing cardiovascular health. Computational approaches offer some non-invasive alternatives to measure blood flow dynamics. Numerical simulations based on traditional methods such as finite-element and other numerical discretizations have been extensively studied and have yielded excellent results. However, adapting these methods to real-life simulations remains a complex task. In this paper, we propose a method that offers flexibility and can efficiently handle real-life simulations. We suggest utilizing the physics-informed neural network (PINN) to solve the Navier-Stokes equation in a deformable domain, specifically addressing the simulation of blood flow in elastic vessels. Our approach models blood flow using an incompressible, viscous Navier-Stokes equation in an Arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian form. The mechanical model for the vessel wall structure is formulated by an equation of Newton's second law of momentum and linear elasticity to the force exerted by the fluid flow. Our method is a mesh-free approach that eliminates the need for discretization and meshing of the computational domain. This makes it highly efficient in solving simulations involving complex geometries. Additionally, with the availability of well-developed open-source machine learning framework packages and parallel modules, our method can easily be accelerated through GPU computing and parallel computing. To evaluate our approach, we conducted experiments on regular cylinder vessels as well as vessels with plaque on their walls. We compared our results to a solution calculated by Finite Element Methods using a dense grid and small time steps, which we considered as the ground truth solution. We report the relative error and the time consumed to solve the problem, highlighting the advantages of our method.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文将PINN应用于弹性血管中的血流模拟，其无网格方法和处理变形域的策略可迁移至生物力学中的FEA替代建模。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address implant design, stress shielding, or multi-objective constrained optimization; it focuses on blood flow in elastic vessels rather than solid mechanics of implants.

summary_zh.motivation: 传统数值方法模拟真实血流计算复杂，需高效灵活方案。
summary_zh.method: 采用PINN求解任意拉格朗日-欧拉形式的Navier-Stokes方程，模拟弹性血管中血流。
summary_zh.result: 在规则圆柱和含斑块血管上，与有限元解对比，误差小且计算时间有优势。
summary_zh.validation: 与密集网格有限元解对比相对误差和耗时。

summary_en.motivation: Traditional numerical simulations of blood flow in deformable vessels are computationally expensive and complex, motivating a meshless, efficient alternative.
summary_en.method: A physics-informed neural network (PINN) solves the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian form, coupled with a linear elasticity model for vessel wall deformation.
summary_en.result: The PINN method achieves low relative error compared to finite element solutions on cylindrical and plaque-containing vessels, with reduced computational time.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed by comparing PINN predictions to high-resolution finite element solutions on benchmark vessel geometries.
